headline: cloudflare/computer
abstract: Give your agent a computer 👾Cloudflare Computer Cloudflare Computer is a virtual filesystem that lives inside a Durable Object. The Durable Object holds the authoritative state in SQLite and exposes one pluggable execution surface through workspace.runtime. Three backends ship today: Container projects the SQLite state into a sandbox container as a real FUSE mount. A sandbox-side daemon (computerd) mounts the state as a filesystem and syncs changes back over a capnweb RPC channel. Full Linux userland, real binaries, real network. Isolate shell runs just-bash in a Dynamic Worker. It reaches the authoritative Workspace over Workers RPC, so there is no second store or sync round trip. Isolate JavaScript runs an ECMAScript module in a fresh Dynamic Worker with structured input/results, durable relative imports, configured libraries, Workspace-backed node:fs/promises, and trusted ws:git and ws:artifacts modules. A Workspace may register multiple backends under stable IDs. workspace.runtime.exec(source, { backend }) is the single execution entry point; the selected backend defines whether source is a shell command or an ECMAScript module. Backends connect lazily on first use. Workspace can also be constructed without a backend at all, giving callers the filesystem on its own. headline: Correct take. 99% of tokens in the world will get consumed in an enterprise context. They will be for writing code, combing through insane amounts of life sciences research, automating manufacturing, securing enterprises, detecting fraud, and thousands of other tasks like this that have significant economic value. This is both where the cost of AI can be most justified but also where the impact of parallel workers doing tasks on your behalf is most useful. Even the agents that most impact consumers will often be wrapped up as just end to end services where the consumer doesn’t think about there being an AI system on the other end, like faster insurance or onboarding to a bank. The key though is it’s going to take years for diffusion of agents across the economy because workflows have to re-engineered to incorporate AI, which is a complete change to how most work happens today. Anyone who’s expecting this to happen overnight should be updating their timelines.

Been thinking about why AI diffusion has been slow. It’s because we are asking users to understand our nerdy lab speak. We greet them with a blank window and ask them to write a prompt. Then they have to pick a model, decide whether they need an agent, and somehow know what context windows, reasoning, MCP, memory, and skills are. Most people don’t care. They need a thing done. If you can give them something that does that, they’re happy. I think we will see that breakthrough product in the next 12 months.

Today we’re announcing SPC Fund IV: $575M to help founders find their life’s work. A decade of guiding founders through -1 to 0 brings @SPC to $2B in AUM and, more importantly, a 1200 member community of the world’s most talented technologists. We strongly believe that: → The person comes before the idea. At -1, generational founders are often busy reading, prototyping, discarding, and earning the right to their own conviction. → Ambition is social. The people you surround yourself with in the early days play a big part in inflecting your ambition. → Patience compounds. It is better to work on something you have deep conviction in rather than simply sprint at the first idea. The quiet months we protect at the beginning have produced three funds in the top 10% of their vintages, and companies like @baseten, @GammaApp, @render, @GoodfireAI, @LumaLabsAI, and @tryprofound. We are proud to have worked with all these founders in their -1 phase and beyond. While we defined -1 to 0, we're no longer bound by it. Fund IV allows us to partner with companies well beyond launch. We're doing this now because we've never seen a wider gap between what's possible and what's being attempted. Intelligence is abundant. The cost of trying ideas keeps falling, and problems that seemed insurmountable a few years ago are quickly becoming solvable. To our members, to the founders who trusted us before anyone else did, and to the LPs who had conviction in our own -1 journey: thank you. This milestone belongs to you as much as to us. To the builders looking to find your life’s work: let’s get started.

High modernism as described by the book Seeing Like A State is the muscular faith of the 19th and early 20th centuries: linear progress, scientific law, technical mastery, rational production, and the belief that nature, including human nature, can be redesigned for greater welfare. In its own historical moment this was not obviously insane. Railroads, electricity, metallurgy, medicine, public health, chemistry, mass production, canals, and sanitation had changed life so violently that awe was rational. High modernism was not only domination. It also “promised freedom from scarcity, want and the arbitrariness of natural calamity.” Seeing Like A State's author was right about the danger of high modernism: when the map can no longer be corrected by the territory, muscular faith becomes catastrophe. But we overlearned the warning. Bring back high-modernist ambition, and add feedback loops. Abundance via superintelligence can be a powerful force making the feedback real. We must dream and build again.
